question: What finally stopped a London colourman selling mummy brown in the 1960s?
answer: Supply, not scruples. C. Roberson & Co., artists' colourmen since the early 1800s, told Time magazine in 1964 that it had no mummy left to grind. The paint mixed ground Egyptian remains with white pitch and myrrh. A colour made from human bodies outlived the Victorians and ended only when the stock room was empty.
